To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the carcinogenic potential of perforated film implants is related to the surface area of the implants and that surface area is more important than the perforation size of the implants.
perforated nitrocelluloses of pore size 3.0 micron and 0.45 microns, respectively, are carcinogenic to mice and that the carcinogenesis of the former is reduced by implanting the film in pairs.
perforations of the implant (film) reduce its carcinogenic potential and increase in surface area of film can compensate for the reduced carcinogenic potential of the perforated film.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of perforated foreign bodies on tumour induction and the mechanisms involved.
the effects of foreign bodies on carcinogenesis and the effects of foreign body perforation size on carcinogenesis.
the effect of film size on the production of foreign body-induced sarcoma by perforation of film implants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carcinogenic effect of a foreign body is a function of its surface area.
the size of the film surface area is a dominant factor in the development of sarcoma on a perforated film.
the carcinogenicity of foreign bodies in mice is dependent on surface area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perforation size is the major determinant of foreign surface sarcomagenicity in rodents and that surface area is the second most important determinant.
film carcinogenesis is a function of film surface area and the number of perforations per unit area.

film carcinogenesis is determined by the product of surface area and perforation size, and that this product may be a measure of the total surface area available for interaction between film and body fluids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
surface area, rather than perforation size, is the main determinant of carcinogenicity of foreign bodies.
surface area is dominant over perforation size in the induction of foreign body sarcomagenesis.
surface area is the key to foreign body sarcoma.
